svg.title: Featured research: The Song or the Self? Within individuals, is self reported emotion during music listening (valence and arousal) linked to EEG band power, beyond what is shared across listeners for the same song? Preregistered before any results were seen, using the MET dataset on OpenNeuro (ds008701): 20 listeners, 20 songs, 66 EEG channels, 395 clean trials. Ratings are split into song consensus and personal deviation: valence is 49 percent song and 47 percent personal, arousal is 67 percent song and 29 percent personal. Three preregistered hypotheses, all not supported: H1, more aroused than usual leads to lower posterior alpha. H2, more pleasant than usual leads to more left frontal activity. H3, people differ in these links. Of 105 exploratory tests, none survived correction. Mixed effects models in R with lme4.

section.h2: The Song or the Self? Personal musical emotion in scalp EEG.
section.p: Within individuals, is self reported emotion during music listening linked to EEG band power, beyond what every listener shares for the same song? Preregistered before any results were seen.

div.p: song consensus (the other listeners) personal deviation
MET dataset, OpenNeuro ds008701. R, lme4, mixed effects models with random intercepts for person and song.

An honest null, reported in full with its limitations.
